commit_message:
[Codegen] Add VectorDistribute constraints for attention

Adds emitVectorDistributeAttentionConstraintsForOp +
buildVectorDistributeAttentionKnobsDict next to the existing
contraction/conv VectorDistribute versions in
LLVMGPUConstraintGenerator, and refactors emitVectorDistributeConstraintsForOp
to branch by op kind so OnlineAttentionOp routes through the new
emitter. emitMMALookup gains an `mmaIdxKnobName` parameter so the two
attention matmuls (QK and PV) carry distinct knobs without colliding
on "mma_idx", and returns the index knob alongside the shape lookups
so layout-binding can reuse it without redeclaring KnobOps.

Knob template (top-level) matches native attention codegen output
(KernelConfig.cpp's setAttention…):
  workgroup          ([1 at batch dims, m_tile on innermost M,
                       n_tile on innermost N])
  reduction          (red_k2 on innermost K2)
  promote_operands   ([0, 1, 2]) + promotion_types
                     ([derived_thread_config]*3)
  decomposition_config
    qk_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
    pv_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
  workgroup_size     ([wg_size_x, 1, 1])
  subgroup_size      (sg_size)

Per-matmul `lowering_config` entries are typed
`IREE::GPU::LoweringConfigAttr`s (not raw DictAttrs — attention
codegen casts them to LoweringConfigAttr, so a raw dict gets silently
rejected and codegen falls back to default per-matmul behavior).
Each carries mma_kind (one_of_knob<qk_mma_idx>/<pv_mma_idx>),
promote_operands + promotion_types (fixed [0,1]/[1] with
derived_thread_config), and subgroup_basis whose counts reference
the top-level sg_m_cnt / sg_n_cnt knobs at the M / N dim positions
(mapping projected per matmul: drop N for QK, drop K1 for PV).

In addition to the per-matmul lowering_config knobs above, the
template declares three SMT-only auxiliary sub-dictionaries that
codegen never reads (the materializer skips them; the verifier
whitelists them):
  smt_internal_subgroup_tile_counts — sg_m_tcnt / sg_n_tcnt / sg_k_tcnt
    factorize m_tile / n_tile / red_k2 into
    (subgroup_count × subgroup_tile_count × intrinsic_size) so the
    schedule-validity helper can reason about each factor.
  smt_internal_mma_layouts — 4 × 6 MMASingleSubgroupLayout fields
    (qk_acc / pv_lhs / pv_rhs / pv_acc each carrying element_x/y,
    thread_x/y, tstrides_x/y) bound to the chosen MMA via
    iree_codegen.smt.lookup ops over qk_mma_idx / pv_mma_idx.
  smt_internal_bools — use_col_major and
    can_reuse_qk_output_for_pv_input, encoded as int_knob ∈ {0, 1}
    (BoolKnobAttr doesn't exist yet); each constrained equivalent to
    a match_layout disjunction over the layout fields above.

Three pieces of generic infrastructure had to learn about typed
wrapper attrs to keep this end-to-end:

1. `hasKnobName` (ConstraintsOp::verify) rewritten with
   AttrTypeWalker so the verifier sees knob references nested inside
   any typed attribute, not just DictionaryAttr/ArrayAttr.

2. `materializeKnobAttribute` (MaterializeSMTConstraintAssignments)
   gains a LoweringConfigAttr case that recurses into the inner
   DictAttr and re-wraps the materialized result.

3. `extractKnobValue` (VerifyPipelineConstraints) gains a
   LoweringConfigAttr case + a generic Attribute-equality `Default`
   for fixed typed leaves like `#iree_gpu.derived_thread_config` in
   per-matmul promotion_types lists. `extractKnobValues` now
   distinguishes intentionally-absent SMT-only auxiliary keys (the
   three `smt_internal_*` sub-dicts) from real config drift: missing
   non-aux entries now fail verification instead of silently
   skipping every constraint that referenced them.

Constraint body ports `generate_attention_vector_distribute_constraints`
(sharktuner/dispatch_constraints.py:434-596) 1:1 — bijective parity
vs the legacy Python tuner is the gate (110 = 110 on the parity
fixture; see the parity-proof snapshots on the tuner side). The body
covers:
  - sg_size == preferred_subgroup_size
  - dim_M / dim_N / dim_K2 each divisible by their tile knobs
  - tile sizes >= pv intrinsic shape and <= 512 (VGPR cap, mirrors
    the matmul emitter)
  - tile-size factorization
    (m_tile == sg_m_cnt × sg_m_tcnt × pv_mma_m, …)
  - QK K1 dim divisible by qk_mma_k
  - sg_m_cnt in [1, 32], sg_n_cnt == 1, sg_num == 4 (Python tuner
    default)
  - QK/PV single-intrinsic_mn invariant
    (qk_mma_m == pv_mma_m, qk_mma_n == pv_mma_n) — mirrors the
    Python tuner's single `intrinsic_mn` SMT variable shared across
    both matmuls
  - 4 × 6 MMA-layout bindings via lookup ops + the
    qk_acc == pv_acc layout-match invariant (the Flash-Attention
    online-attention requirement that QK's output and PV's output
    live in the same per-subgroup layout)
  - use_col_major / can_reuse_qk_output_for_pv_input equivalences
    against the match_layout disjunctions on those bindings
  - per-matmul tile-based shared-memory budget with the
    `If(can_reuse, pv_shared / 2, pv_shared)` reuse term (matching
    Python's `pv_shared //= 2` approximation on reuse — exact for
    square tiles, slightly off otherwise)
  - is_valid_vector_distribute_mma_schedule (schedule_aligned +
    lhs/rhs distributable) for both QK and PV schedules

Decomposition-config also flows back to the tuner via a parallel
C++/C/Python helper triad:
  - materializeDecompositionConfigFromConstraints in
    MaterializeSMTConstraintAssignments (kDecompositionConfigKey
    promoted to SMTConstraintUtils.h so the emitter and materializer
    share one source of truth)
  - C API ireeCodegenMaterializeDecompositionConfigFromConstraintsOp
    (mirror of the existing ...CompilationInfoFromConstraintsOp)
  - Symbol exports in api_exports.{ld,def,macos.lst,c}
  - Python binding iree_codegen.materialize_decomposition_config

Other deferrals: only square-MN MMAs (m == n) are enumerated for the
attention path so the constraint body can use a single intrinsic_mn
variable; supporting non-square MMAs (e.g. VDMFMA_F32_8x16x64x2_F16)
is follow-up work that needs a paired (intrinsic_m, intrinsic_n)
variable. inferAttentionDimInfo asserts the v0 single-dim-per-role
restriction (m / n / k1 / k2 each contributing exactly one loop dim)
so multi-head shapes with multiple M dims fail loudly rather than
silently dropping outer dims.

Test coverage:
  - new config_llvm_gpu_vd_attention_constraints.mlir locks in the
    attention knob template (typed per-matmul LoweringConfigAttr
    with mma_kind/promote_operands/promotion_types/subgroup_basis,
    SMT-internal aux sub-dicts) plus CHECK-DAG for every constraint
    family (tile/factorization, sg counts, single-intrinsic_mn,
    layout bindings × 24, qk_acc == pv_acc invariant, use_col_major
    and can_reuse bools, schedule-validity for QK and PV).
  - verify_smt_constraints_e2e.mlir gets attention passing +
    violation splits in the new schema; passing case uses
    asymmetric m_tile / n_tile (128 / 64) so accidental axis swaps
    in the emitter would surface as verification failures rather
    than silently passing under symmetry.
  - tuner_api_test.py gets attention round-trips through both
    iree_codegen.materialize_compilation_info and the new
    iree_codegen.materialize_decomposition_config (happy path,
    indexed MMA selection, missing-assignment error).

Issue: https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/23535
Signed-off-by: Bangtian Liu <liubangtian@gmail.com>
